name: Shop_SelectPartyMemberItem
domain: Runs the shop's two-stage party-member and owned-item selection flow and returns both selections to the caller.
notes: Recovered from the retained owner, its local callers, the byte-exact Shop_SelectPartyMember template, and the established ShopRuntime layout.
The candidate deliberately names every recovered local role; generated register and stack-slot identifiers are not retained as source vocabulary.
The typed semantic reconstruction improves the repaired raw m2c result from 232 differing halfwords and 184 wrong instructions to 190 and 70 respectively.

A 5,000-candidate safe family-template walk reduced the ranking score to 101 structural rows and 187 differing halfwords but did not produce an exact object; its generated temporary spelling is retained only in the ignored search workspace.
Exact-C adoption remains gated on an independently compiled zero-difference object.

This session's re-inspection confirms the residual is register-allocation drift, not a spelling gap: at the Func_080150c8 call the reference reloads its 5th argument from the [sp,#4] stack slot (the 'result' local, spilled there in the prologue) while the candidate supplies it from a live register, and the candidate/reference disagree on which of redraw/result/unit_id occupies the stack slot vs r9 vs fp after the prologue's three zero/one stores. Reordering the local declarations so 'result' is declared before 'redraw' (testing whether declaration order drives pseudo-register numbering) was tried and made the score strictly worse (191 differing_halfwords, 76 wrong_instructions, reverted).

Separately, this session found a genuine callee bug in the prior candidate: the cursor-positioning call at reference offset 0x67 (bl target 0xffffd5dc, i.e. Func_080b0a20) was being reconstructed via shop.h's Shop_SetCursorPosition macro (Func_080b09fc, a different, unrelated 4-argument function) rather than the actual 3-argument Func_080b0a20(cursor, target_x, target_y) the reference calls. Declaring Func_080b0a20 directly and calling it with the 3 arguments the assembly actually passes (r0=&shop->cursor, r1=-32, r2=112, with no live r3 argument) makes that one bl instruction match the reference exactly in the aligned diff. This is real, verified-correct groundwork for the next attempt even though the headline count moved from 190/70 to 192/70: fixing the wrong callee removed a phantom 4th argument setup that had been coincidentally absorbing some of the length/alignment mismatch caused by the (still unresolved) register-spill gap documented above. Also re-pointed the two literal-0 arguments in the Func_080a1028 call to the 'result' variable, matching the reference's ldr-from-[sp,#4] read at that site; this was score-neutral (GCC keeps 'result' in fp for the candidate regardless of the C spelling) but is more evidence-true. The candidate.c now calls the verified-correct Func_080b0a20 callee; the remaining gap is still the same compiler-internals register/spill assignment identified above and needs permuter-style search, not manual respelling.

2026-08-27 session: re-verified current score is 192 differing_halfwords / 70 wrong_instructions / candidate 484 vs reference 488 (4 bytes / 1 Thumb insn short). Ran the m2c workbench against the retained assembly to get a real decompilation (out/workbench/080b3444/m2c/080b3444.c): it confirms this candidate's control-flow shape (redraw-gated block, then an INPUT_NEW_KEYS&1 / &2 / repeat-key three-way split, all via one shared loop test) is structurally right, and that 'selected_index' (m2c's var_r7_83) is set to 0 as a plain statement immediately before the loop rather than at its declaration -- but moving that single init down (with or without also reshuffling the redraw/unit_id/result declaration order) reliably made the score worse (480-492 bytes, 76-166 wrong_instructions), never better, so it was reverted. Also tried, each independently reverted after measuring: (a) rewriting the three sequential `if`+continue/break checks as an explicit if/else-if/else chain matching m2c's shape exactly -- byte-for-byte score-neutral (this GCC's CFG builder treats the two forms identically here, so this is not the missing structural piece); (b) replacing the `for(;;)`+continue/break with the literal `loop_1:`/`goto loop_1` label form m2c emits (the technique that fixed a different sibling, 08029554) -- this made things substantially worse (492 bytes, 148 wrong_instructions) and additionally caused the compiler to stop keeping 'shop' in r8 at all (moved it to r7), so the goto form is actively harmful for this owner, not neutral; (c) an exhaustive-feeling sweep of every local-declaration ordering of {selected_index, redraw, unit_id, item_slot, result} that preserves 'selected_index' as the first declared/initialized local: every ordering tried lands on the exact same 192/70/484 optimum UNLESS 'unit_id' is declared before 'redraw', or 'result' is declared before everything else, both of which regress to a worse (488-byte, ~82-86-wrong) local optimum with a still-wrong register/stack mapping -- so 192/70/484 looks like a genuine local floor for pure declaration-order search, not an unexplored corner. Also confirmed (via a byte-identical no-op result) that swapping the Func_080150c8/Func_080a1028 call-site zero arguments between the literal 0 and the 'result' variable is completely score-neutral, i.e. GCC's value numbering already treats them as interchangeable regardless of source spelling -- not a useful lever. Net: the file was left unchanged from the prior session's 192/70/484 state; the missing 4 bytes is still believed to live in the same result/redraw/unit_id register-vs-[sp,#4] assignment gap described above (reference reloads 'result' from the stack via an explicit `add r0,sp,#4; ldrb r0,[r0,#0]` byte-load at the Func_080b0a20 cursor-anchor field write, where this candidate instead forwards an already-live register holding the same value 0 -- i.e. reference has strictly more register pressure or a different live-range shape around that point than any declaration reordering tried here reproduces), and probably needs either a genuinely different intervening statement (something that keeps 'result' truly dead in a register a beat longer) or bounded PERM_GENERAL search over the handful of call-argument/statement-order choices identified above rather than further manual declaration permutation.
